basis: Defined by deficient factor V activity and impaired blood coagulation; immune causation is not universal across the umbrella.
Isolated inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with ventricular dysfunction and conduction abnormalities.
Tumour originates in the uterine cervix, a reproductive organ outside the axes; mesenchymal differentiation does not establish musculoskeletal involvement.
Nervous system and renal tubules are major targets of heavy-metal toxicity; patterns vary by metal. Acute gastrointestinal symptoms alone do not establish lasting injury.
Purine metabolism defect causes immunodeficiency; direct neurologic abnormalities occur in 30-79%. Autoimmune cytopenias and infections are separately diagnosed conditions.
Sweat gland tumour umbrella predominantly involving cutaneous appendages; breast and ceruminous examples do not justify additional axes across the group.
Congenital retinal phototransduction dysfunction causes stationary night blindness; nervous-system ancestry does not establish extraocular disease.
Neoplastic polyposis umbrella supported by intestinal and gastric polyposis children; lesions occupy gastrointestinal mucosa.
Cardiomyopathy/septal defects occur in 30-79%; diaphragmatic defects in 80-99% and mandibular aplasia/hypoplasia in 30-79%. Hearing impairment and brain abnormalities are <30%.
Epilepsy, spastic diplegia and intellectual disability define a neurologic syndrome; spasticity does not establish primary skeletal muscle disease.
Defined by reduced lung volume and impaired ventilation; extrapulmonary causes vary and do not establish another affected axis across the umbrella.
Exposure causes corneal and conjunctival surface injury; this is not inherently infectious or immune-mediated.
Skeletal dysplasia affects vertebrae, epiphyses, metaphyses and joints, with common osteoarthritis and impaired mobility.
The umbrella explicitly comprises neurodevelopmental disease and vitreoretinopathy; retinal vascular abnormalities belong to the ocular phenotype.
Ataxia, intellectual disability, optic atrophy and skin anomalies define CAMOS; renal insufficiency/nephrotic phenotype occurs in 30-79%. Cutaneous vascular axis omitted by cap.
Chronic gonococcal infection of seminal vesicles; infection supplies an axis, while the affected reproductive organ is outside the organ axes.
Antral endocrine G-cell hyperfunction causes hypergastrinemia and defining duodenal ulceration.
Selective antibody immunodeficiency; most patients are asymptomatic, and predisposition to respiratory or autoimmune diseases does not establish organ damage.
Defined by absent vasa deferentia and male infertility, outside the axes; shared CFTR causation does not establish cystic fibrosis organ involvement.
Cranial nerve disease umbrella; ocular and auditory disease apply to particular nerve subtypes rather than most patients across the group.
CASPR2 antibody-mediated encephalitis affects central and peripheral nervous systems; dysautonomia does not by itself establish other organ damage.
Congenital erythrocytosis defines the disease. Thrombosis and hemorrhage are risks; the single annotated pulmonary hypertension case cannot establish common involvement.
Peripheral corneal degeneration and thinning cause substantial astigmatism; no systemic immune mechanism is established.
Glaucoma damages the eye and optic nerve; varied secondary causes do not establish a shared extraocular or immune axis.
Cancer susceptibility does not establish current organ damage; principal predisposed sites are breast and reproductive organs, while pancreatic and other cancers are later risks.
